set.st: Hugo, Albert and Rudolph Donnerstag were arrested near Rhinelander in August 1908 for making counterfeit $5 gold pieces and silver; agents found $1,035 in spurious gold coin, plaster molds, lathes and a plating outfit, and 11 guns in the house. The mother tried to get away in a boat, so the home was on a lake; Hugo and Albert's place was about 18 miles out and Rudolph lived nearer the city. On Oct. 25 the three sawed a bar and went down a rope from the Dane County jail. They went straight home, and the Madison papers (Nov. 5) said it was because a pot of gold, $4,000 in gold coin, was secreted in the woods and they feared forest fires would destroy it. Hugo and Albert gave up at Rudolph's house about twelve miles from Rhinelander; Rudolph was shot in both legs while running through the woods near Manson Lake, eight miles west of the city, near the old Donnerstag home. None of the papers read says the $4,000 was dug up, and since they were coiners it may have been their own make. The local weekly places the family: in 1905 Rudolph Donnerstag 'of the town of Woodboro' was in court over a gun threat, and in September 1908 Hugo wrote from the Madison jail; he had earlier served time for killing his father. Pin is approximate (town or township only), not the spot itself.
set.t: Look for the 1908-14 Oneida County plat book or tax roll to find the Donnerstag land (town of Woodboro, which the 1905 paper names), then old cellar holes and the woods edge around it. Any gold coins of 1900-08 from there should be weighed and rung: counterfeits were cast and plated. Permission: private or county forest land, ask first.
pinev: Placed on Manson Lake (GNIS 45.5625, -89.6329) from 'near Manson lake, eight miles west' (Eagle River Review, Nov. 13, 1908); the house itself is not yet placed.
Rudolph Donnerstag was 'of the town of Woodboro' in 1905 (Rhinelander New North, 14 Sep 1905), which takes in Manson Lake; the land itself is not yet on a plat.
